result.title: A .github governed-intake release merge can silently break the deployed github-mcp-worker (consumer pin mismatch → verifyLiveManifest commit_mismatch)

direction-checked-at: 2026-10-19T04:35:00Z
## Work type
Defect

## Current executable scope — accepted no-pins direction

The accepted ruling is [Code#8197 comment6051567438](https://github.com/spencer-shadley/code/issues/8197#issuecomment-6051567438): Spencer said, "We shouldn't even have pins at all." [Code#7658's bounded settlement](https://github.com/spencer-shadley/code/issues/7658#issuecomment-6169153046) assigns pin-file removal to #7658, consumer-pin check wiring removal to #8036, and retained post-merge observability to #8070.

This issue retains the outage evidence and the outcome that producer publication must not break the governed-intake consumer through obsolete pin matching. Its former consumer-pin gate, staged-pin promotion, paired-pin merge prerequisites and October 13 human-decision wait are withdrawn. No new pin or gate is commissioned here.

Current acceptance:
- Preserve the historical incident and recovery evidence below.
- Reconcile the surviving consumer-availability outcome with #7658 and #8036 after their removal work lands; do not close this issue merely because one removal PR merged.
- Retain useful post-merge observability with #8070 without restoring pin comparison.
- Preserve existing implementation custody. The bounded #7658 settlement does not establish exhaustive direction-audit completion or authorize another writer.

The historical design sections identified below are retained for learning only and are not executable requirements.

## What happened or what is needed?
A merge in `spencer-shadley/.github` that correctly republishes the governed-intake release can still silently break the deployed `github-mcp-worker`. The worker pins one exact producer release (`tools/work-spine/governed-intake-worker-published-release.pin.json`). On every create, triage, completion and health request, `verifyLiveManifest` (`tools/github-mcp-worker/src/triage-checklist-state.ts`) compares the live `.github` main manifest with that pin and fails closed with `governed-intake commit_mismatch` (or `digest_mismatch`) on any other identity, including a new **same-revision** republish. Nothing before the merge checks the consumer pin, so the outage starts at merge time and lasts until someone notices and reverts or re-pins and redeploys.

## Initial priority guess
P1

## Why this initial priority?
This has caused a fleet-wide governed-intake outage twice in two days. docs/guides/issue-priority.md: high frequency × fleet-wide severity.
